**What parking does here:**
- **Stage 2 (Closure notices)** parks, even though Track B doesn't depend on the study. You asked to park the whole roadmap, so it goes to the backlog with the rest.
- **Track A's Ranked list (O2, O3, O4)** parks, one deferred item each.
- **Stage 2's text-message notices** are not a stage or a list item, so they don't get a deferred item.
- **There is no spec, methodology or critique file**, so nothing retires alongside the roadmap. The Stage 1 findings file stays where it is, since it's a shipped result.

**Step 1: read the deferred-item schema, and check for an existing backlog.**

```
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/references/deferred-backlog.md
Read specs/deferred_items.md        # may not exist
```

**Step 2: append to `specs/deferred_items.md`.** I'll fit the wording to the schema once I've read it. In outline:

```markdown
## lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06

- [ ] Closure notices (parked Stage 2, Track B). Boat operators get an email notice within an hour of a lock closing, built on the closure log's live feed. Size: small (one closure-log poll each 10 minutes). Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address on the list within an hour of a new closure entry.
- [ ] 7-day closure-risk outlook per lock (O2, Track A Ranked list #1). Builds on Stage 1's response curve: closure is rare below a gauge level of 3.1 m and reaches about 60% at 3.8 m (specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md). Size: small (one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min on a laptop). Done when: a 7-day closure-risk outlook for each lock is produced from the river-level forecast.
- [ ] Per-lock closure curves, pooled across all 14 locks (O3, Track A Ranked list #2). Stage 1 found the four longest-record locks show close to the same curve. Size: large (about 14 times Stage 1's 1.8 GB, so roughly 25 GB; fit time unmeasured). Done when: separate closure curves for all 14 locks, pooled across locks, are fit on real data.
- [ ] Closure-history map for boat operators (O4, Track A Ranked list #3). Size: about a day (one static map page). Done when: a closure-history map of the canal's locks is published for boat operators.
```

**Step 3: mark and move the roadmap.**

Add this line under the header of `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md`:

> PARKED (2026-11-06) — 1 of 2 stages complete. Remaining stage and Track A's Ranked list parked to specs/deferred_items.md, section `lock-closures-roadmap — 2026-11-06`.

Then move and commit:

```
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: 1 of 2 stages complete (study funding ended)"
```

The commit goes on `main` locally, with no push. I'll report back with the commit hash and the final deferred-item text once these run.

If funding returns, the four items are self-contained in the backlog. The outlook (O2) is the cheapest restart, because Stage 1's curve already exists.
